'''''Agave victoriae-reginae''''', the '''[[Queen Victoria]] agave''' or '''royal agave''', is a small [[species]] of [[succulent plant|succulent]] flowering [[perennial plant]], noted for its streaks of white on sculptured geometrical leaves, and popular as an ornamental.

This agave is highly variable in form, but in general the rosettes are small and compact, growing to 0.5m, composed of short, rigid, thick leaves that are green with a pattern of distinctive white markings. The markings are generally along leaf keels or margins, giving a sort of polyhedral appearance. Marginal teeth are usually lacking, while the terminus of the leaf may include 1 to 3 spines, each 1.5–3 cm in length. Cream coloured flowers are borne in erect [[racemes]] up to 4m in length.

''A. victoriae-reginae'' is found in the [[Chihuahuan Desert]] in the Mexican States of [[Coahuila]], [[Durango]] and [[Nuevo León]], with about a half-dozen subspecies named. The situation is complicated by hybrids with a number of other agave species.<ref>[[Howard Scott Gentry]], ''Agaves of Continental North America'' (University of Arizona Press, 1982) pp. 183–185</ref><ref>Moore, Thomas. Gardeners' Chronicle, new series 4: 485. 1875.</ref> Although it faces some local threats, the population of the species as a whole is stable, and it is not considered by the [[IUCN]] to be threatened.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

It is cold-hardy as agaves go, and thus finds favor as a small accent in many northerly gardens. However it is recommended in the UK that this plant be kept in heated conditions under glass during winter. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/698/Agave-victoriae-reginae/Details |title=RHS Plant Selector Agave victoriae-reginae AGM / RHS Gardening |publisher=Apps.rhs.org.uk |date= |access-date=2020-03-12}}</ref> When grown as a houseplant, it is best planted in a very porous, sandy soil and given direct sunlight or bright shade. The soil should be permitted to dry out between waterings. The plant need only be repotted about every two to three years. Propagation is normally by seed, since the plant rarely produces basal shoots.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Chiusoli |first1=Alessandro |last2=Boriani |first2=Luisa Maria |title=Simon & Schuster's guide to houseplants |date=1986 |publisher=Simon and Schuster |location=New York |isbn=0-671-63131-4}}</ref>
